\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Low Degree Obstruction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.RazborovSmolensky.LowDegreeObstruction
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This file completes the counting half of the Razborov--Smolensky $\mathrm{MOD}\,q$ lower
bound over the root cube $\{1,\omega\}^n \subseteq K^n$.  It introduces a concrete finite
candidate family --- squarefree polynomials whose supports all have size at most $D$ ---
proves that it is complete for degree-$\le D$ polynomials on the cube, counts the cube,
the candidate family, and Hamming balls of functions, and combines these into an explicit
obstruction to low-degree approximation of the product $\prod_i x_i$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Low-degree squarefree supports]
\lean{ACP.LowDegreeSupport}
\label{ACP.LowDegreeSupport}
\leanok
For $n, D \in \mathbb{N}$, the type of supports of squarefree monomials of degree at most
$D$: the subtype of finsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$.  In the
displays below this type is written $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Low-degree squarefree polynomial from coefficients]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.squarefreeMonomial}
Given coefficients $c$ indexed by $\texttt{ACP.LowDegreeSupport}\ n\ D$, the multivariate
polynomial
\[
\sum_{\substack{s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n \\ \abs{s} \le D}} c(s)\, \prod_{i \in s} X_i ,
\]
i.e. the sum of the squarefree monomials $\texttt{ACP.squarefreeMonomial}\ s$ weighted by
$c$, with the terms of support size $> D$ set to $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Squarefree polynomial representation on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.exists_squarefree_representative_on_rootCube}
\label{ACP.exists_squarefree_representative_on_rootCube}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.squarefreeMonomial, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
\difficulty{7}
Let $K$ be a field, fix an element $\omega \in K$, and let $n$ be a natural number.
Write $\{1,\omega\}^n$ for the set of vectors $x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)$ with each coordinate
$x_i \in \{1,\omega\}$. Then for every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ there exist
coefficients $c_S \in K$, indexed by the subsets $S \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$, such that
the squarefree (multilinear) polynomial
\[
  P(X_1,\dots,X_n) \;=\; \sum_{S} c_S \prod_{i \in S} X_i
\]
satisfies $P(x) = f(x)$ for every $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Low-degree monomials multilinearize on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.monomial_lowDegree_squarefree_complete_on_rootCube}
\label{ACP.monomial_lowDegree_squarefree_complete_on_rootCube}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial, ACP.rootCube, ACP.squarefreeMonomial}
\difficulty{6}
Let $K$ be a field and let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \ne 1$. Fix $n, D \in \bbn$,
and consider a monomial $a\,X^m$ in the variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ over $K$, given by an
exponent vector $m : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbn$ and a coefficient $a \in K$, whose total
degree $\sum_i m_i$ is at most $D$. Then there exist coefficients $c : \mathcal{S}_{n,D}
\to K$, indexed by the squarefree supports $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s}
\le D$, such that the squarefree polynomial $\sum_{\abs{s} \le D} c(s)\prod_{i \in s}
X_i$ takes the same value as $a\,X^m$ at every point $x$ of the root cube
$\{1,\omega\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Additivity of the coefficient-to-polynomial map]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_add}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_add}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a field $K$ and natural numbers $n$ and $D$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ be the set
of subsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$. For a coefficient
function $c \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, write $P(c) = \sum_{s \in
\mathcal{S}_{n,D}} c(s)\, \prod_{i \in s} X_i$ for the associated squarefree polynomial
in $K[X_i : i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n]$. Then for any two coefficient functions $c_1, c_2
\colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$ one has \[ P(c_1 + c_2) = P(c_1) + P(c_2), \] where $c_1
+ c_2$ denotes the pointwise sum.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Zero coefficients yield the zero polynomial]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_zero}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_zero}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial}
\difficulty{2}
Let $K$ be a field and let $n, D \in \bbn$. Applying the low-degree squarefree
polynomial construction to the identically zero coefficient function on
$\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ produces the zero element of the polynomial ring $K[X_0, \dots,
X_{n-1}]$; that is,
\[
\sum_{\substack{s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n \\ \abs{s} \le D}} 0 \cdot \prod_{i \in s}
X_i \;=\; 0 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Additivity in the coefficients]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_sum}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_sum}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_add, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a field $K$ and natural numbers $n, D$, and write $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ for the type
of subsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$. For a coefficient
function $c \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, let $P(c)$ denote the multivariate
polynomial $\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}_{n,D}} c(s)\, \prod_{i \in s} X_i$ over $K$ in the
variables $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$. Then for any finite index set $S$ and any family of
coefficient functions $(c_i)_{i \in S}$ with each $c_i \colon \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$,
the polynomial built from the pointwise sum of coefficients equals the sum of the
individual polynomials:
\[
P\!\left(\sum_{i \in S} c_i\right) = \sum_{i \in S} P(c_i).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness of low-degree squarefree polynomials on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.lowDegree_squarefree_complete_on_rootCube}
\label{ACP.lowDegree_squarefree_complete_on_rootCube}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_sum, ACP.monomial_lowDegree_squarefree_complete_on_rootCube, ACP.rootCube}
\difficulty{5}
Let $K$ be a field and let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \ne 1$. For natural numbers
$n$ and $D$, write $\{1,\omega\}^n$ for the set of vectors $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$
each of whose coordinates equals $1$ or $\omega$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ be the
collection of finsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$. Then for every
polynomial $Q \in K[X_i : i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n]$ of total degree at most $D$, there
exist coefficients $c : \mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$ such that the squarefree polynomial
$\sum_{\abs{s} \le D} c(s)\,\prod_{i \in s} X_i$ agrees with $Q$ at every point of
$\{1,\omega\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Total degree bound for a low-degree squarefree polynomial]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_totalDegree_le}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial_totalDegree_le}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial, ACP.squarefreeMonomial, ACP.squarefreeMonomial_totalDegree_le_card}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K$ be a field and fix $n, D \in \bbn$. For any assignment of coefficients $c \colon
\mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K$, indexed by the subsets $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with
$\abs{s} \le D$, the polynomial
\[
\sum_{\substack{s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n \\ \abs{s} \le D}} c(s)\, \prod_{i \in s}
X_i \in K[X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}]
\]
has total degree at most $D$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Support-to-sigma injection]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSupportSigmaMap}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSupportSigmaMap}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport}
The map sending a low-degree support $s$ to the pair consisting of its exact cardinality
$\abs{s} \in \mathrm{Fin}(D+1)$ together with $s$ itself, viewed as an element of
$\{t : \mathrm{Finset}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n) \mid \abs{t} = \abs{s}\}$.  It is used as an
injection for the binomial-sum bound rather than as a full equivalence.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Binomial-sum bound on low-degree supports]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeSupport_card_le_binomial_sum}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeSupport_card_le_binomial_sum}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeCoeff_card, ACP.lowDegreeSupportSigmaMap}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $D$, let $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ denote the (finite) type of
low-degree squarefree supports on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, that is, the subsets $s \subseteq
\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ with $\abs{s} \le D$. Then the number of such supports satisfies
\[
\abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,D}} \;\le\; \sum_{t=0}^{D} \binom{n}{t}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality of the space of coefficient functions]
\lean{ACP.lowDegreeCoeff_card}
\label{ACP.lowDegreeCoeff_card}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport}
\difficulty{1}
Fix natural numbers $n$ and $D$, and write $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ for the type of supports
of squarefree monomials of degree at most $D$ in $n$ variables. For any finite type
$K_0$, the number of functions from $\mathcal{S}_{n,D}$ to $K_0$ is
\[
\abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K_0} \;=\; \abs{K_0}^{\,\abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,D}}}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Root cube as Boolean strings]
\lean{ACP.rootCubeEquivFinTwo}
\label{ACP.rootCubeEquivFinTwo}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube}
If $\omega \ne 1$, the explicit equivalence $\{1,\omega\}^n \simeq (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to
\mathrm{Fin}\,2)$ that records, for each coordinate, whether its value is $1$ or $\omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality of the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_card_of_ne_one}
\label{ACP.rootCube_card_of_ne_one}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeEquivFinTwo}
\difficulty{2}
Let $K$ be a finite field and let $\omega \in K$ with $\omega \ne 1$. Then the root cube
$\{1,\omega\}^n$, consisting of those vectors $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$ with $x_i \in
\{1,\omega\}$ for every coordinate $i$, has exactly $2^n$ elements.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Counting functions on the root-of-unity cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_function_card_of_ne_one}
\label{ACP.rootCube_function_card_of_ne_one}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCube_card_of_ne_one}
\difficulty{2}
Let $K$ be a finite field, let $\omega \in K$ with $\omega \ne 1$, and let $n \in \bbn$.
Writing $\{1,\omega\}^n$ for the set of vectors $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$ each of
whose coordinates equals $1$ or $\omega$, the number of functions $\{1,\omega\}^n \to K$
is \[ \abs{K}^{\,2^n}. \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Hamming-ball bound for function spaces]
\lean{ACP.function_hammingBall_card_le_binomial}
\label{ACP.function_hammingBall_card_le_binomial}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite types, fix a function $\mathrm{center} : \alpha \to
\beta$, and let $e \in \bbn$. Then the number of functions $f : \alpha \to \beta$ that
disagree with $\mathrm{center}$ on at most $e$ points of $\alpha$ — that is, for which
$\abs{\{a \in \alpha : \mathrm{center}(a) \ne f(a)\}} \le e$ — satisfies
\[
\abs{\{\, f : \alpha \to \beta \;:\; \abs{\{a \in \alpha : \mathrm{center}(a) \ne
f(a)\}} \le e \,\}} \;\le\; \sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{\abs{\alpha}}{t}\,\abs{\beta}^{\,t}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Volume bound for a Hamming ball on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCubeBall_card_le_binomial}
\label{ACP.rootCubeBall_card_le_binomial}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.function_hammingBall_card_le_binomial, ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBall, ACP.rootCubeFunctionBadCount}
\difficulty{2}
Let $K$ be a finite field, let $\omega \in K$, and let $n, e \in \bbn$. Write
$\{1,\omega\}^n$ for the root cube of vectors $x : \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to K$ each of whose
coordinates equals $1$ or $\omega$, and consider functions $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$,
the Hamming distance between two such functions being the number of points of the cube
on which they differ. For any function $\mathrm{center} : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$, the
number of functions whose Hamming distance from $\mathrm{center}$ is at most $e$
satisfies
\[
\abs{\{\, f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K \;\mid\; f \text{ differs from } \mathrm{center}
\text{ on at most } e \text{ points}\,\}}
  \;\le\; \sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{\,\abs{\{1,\omega\}^n}\,}{t}\,\abs{K}^{\,t},
\]
where $\abs{\{1,\omega\}^n}$ is the number of points of the cube and $\abs{K}$ is the
number of elements of $K$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Counting obstruction for low-degree squarefree approximation on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_counting_obstruction_lowDegreeSquarefree}
\label{ACP.rootCube_counting_obstruction_lowDegreeSquarefree}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.lowDegreeSquarefreePolynomial, ACP.lowDegree_squarefree_complete_on_rootCube, ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBadCount, ACP.rootCubeBall, ACP.rootCubeBall_card_le_binomial, ACP.rootCube_card_of_ne_one, ACP.rootCube_counting_obstruction, ACP.rootCube_function_card_of_ne_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $K$ be a finite field, let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \neq 1$, and fix natural
numbers $n, D, e, B$. Suppose the ball bound
\[
\sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{2^n}{t}\,\abs{K}^{\,t} \;\le\; B
\]
holds, together with the strict counting inequality
\[
\abs{K}^{\,2^n} \;>\; \abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,D} \to K}\cdot B .
\]
Then it is \emph{not} the case that every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ admits a
multivariate polynomial $Q \in K[X_i : i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n]$ of total degree at most
$D$ that disagrees with $f$ on at most $e$ points of the cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$; that is,
some $f$ fails to be approximated in this sense by any such $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No low-degree approximation of the coordinate product on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.no_low_degree_rootProd_approx_concrete}
\label{ACP.no_low_degree_rootProd_approx_concrete}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.LowDegreeSupport, ACP.exists_squarefree_representative_on_rootCube, ACP.no_low_degree_rootProd_approx, ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBadCount, ACP.rootCube_counting_obstruction_lowDegreeSquarefree, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
\difficulty{2}
Let $K$ be a finite field and let $\omega \in K$ satisfy $\omega \neq 0$ and $\omega
\neq 1$, and fix natural numbers $n, d, e, B$. Suppose that
\[
  \sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{2^{n}}{t}\,\abs{K}^{t} \;\le\; B
\]
and that
\[
  \abs{K}^{2^{n}} \;>\; \abs{\,\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor + d} \to K\,}\cdot B ,
\]
where $\abs{\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor + d} \to K}$ is the number of functions
from $\mathcal{S}_{n,\lfloor n/2\rfloor + d}$ to $K$. Then there is no polynomial $P \in
K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ of total degree at most $d$ whose bad count against the coordinate
product $x \mapsto \prod_{i} x_i$ on the root cube $\{1,\omega\}^{n}$ is at most $e$;
that is, every such $P$ disagrees with $\prod_i x_i$ at more than $e$ points of
$\{1,\omega\}^n$.
\end{theorem}
